NFL DFS Wide Receiver Rankings: Week 5 (DraftKings)

DraftKings main slate · Sunday, October 11 · 11 games · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of October 10, 10:04 PM ET

Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the top-projected wide receiver on the Week 5 DraftKings main slate at 21.1 DraftKings points for $8,800, against San Francisco. Amon-Ra St. Brown (19.3, $7,900) and Ja'Marr Chase (18.8, $8,100) are next.

Tre' Harris returns the most per dollar among wide receivers projected for at least 9 points: 3.23 projected points per $1,000 at $4,100.

Every projection is a SPAGS model estimate from the October 10, 10:04 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. This page updates each time the main-slate numbers are published.

Wide receivers to know in Week 5

Jaxon Smith-Njigba, SEA vs SF ($8,800)

Jaxon Smith-Njigba carries the highest SPAGS model projection at the position, 21.1 DraftKings points at $8,800, the 2nd-highest on the entire main slate. That is 1.8 points clear of Amon-Ra St. Brown. The model gives him 8.5 targets on 24.3 routes. The salary works out to 2.39 projected points per $1,000, 7th of 31 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Smith-Njigba averaged 21.0 points with a simulated floor of 9.2 and a ceiling of 41.4, and he holds 17% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Seattle is a 3-point favorite at home against San Francisco, with an implied team total of 24.25 in a game totaled at 45.5.

Amon-Ra St. Brown, DET at ARI ($7,900)

Amon-Ra St. Brown projects 2nd at the position with 19.3 DraftKings points at $7,900. The model gives him 9.3 targets on 34.6 routes. The salary works out to 2.44 projected points per $1,000, 5th of 31 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Brown averaged 19.4 points with a simulated floor of 7.8 and a ceiling of 39.9, and he holds 21% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Detroit is a 5.5-point favorite on the road against Arizona, with an implied team total of 30 in a game totaled at 54.5.

Ja'Marr Chase, CIN at MIA ($8,100)

Ja'Marr Chase projects 3rd at the position with 18.8 DraftKings points at $8,100. The model gives him 7.7 targets on 35.5 routes. The salary works out to 2.32 projected points per $1,000, 9th of 31 at the position. Across 50,000 simulations Chase averaged 18.9 points with a simulated floor of 7.1 and a ceiling of 38.9, and he holds 6% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. Cincinnati is a 7-point favorite on the road against Miami, with an implied team total of 25.25 in a game totaled at 43.5.

Value: Tre' Harris, LAC vs DEN ($4,100)

Tre' Harris projects for 13.3 DraftKings points at $4,100, which works out to 3.23 points per $1,000 of salary. That is the best rate of any player priced in the cheaper half of the 31 wide receivers the model projects for 9 or more points. The model gives him 8.8 targets on 25.3 routes. Across 50,000 simulations Harris averaged 13.2 points with a simulated floor of 2.5 and a ceiling of 33.5, and he holds 23% of the simulated winning-lineup credit. The Chargers are a 3.5-point underdog at home against Denver, with an implied team total of 19 in a game totaled at 41.5.
